artworks.title: The Minotaur
artworks.description: Watts paints the bull-headed beast alone on a parapet, staring out to sea for the Athenian tribute ship, a crushed bird under its fist. The Tate canvas turns the Cretan monster into a Victorian allegory of predatory lust — the Minotaur waiting for victims, not yet facing Theseus.

artworks.title: Theseus Killing the Minotaur
artworks.description: In a small oil on panel, Cima stages the labyrinth's climax: Theseus drives his blade into the Minotaur's body while the bull-man's hybrid form collapses. Now in the Museo Poldi Pezzoli, Milan (on deposit from the Pinacoteca di Brera), the intimate scene distills the Cretan combat into a Renaissance cabinet piece.

artworks.title: Theseus Slaying the Minotaur
artworks.description: Barye, master of animal anatomy, casts the Minotaur as a wrestling adversary forced to the ground — bull head and human torso locked under Theseus' weight. The 1843 bronze fuses Romantic vigor with the myth's most physical image of the beast's death; Baltimore Museum of Art.

artworks.title: Theseus Victorious over the Minotaur
artworks.description: From the House of M. Gavius Rufus at Pompeii, this fresco shows the Minotaur crumpled at Theseus' feet while freed youths crowd to thank the hero. The bull-headed corpse is the painting's dark centre — the labyrinth's monster made domestic decoration for a Roman atrium. Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli (inv. 9043).

films.title: Immortals
films.description: Tarsem's labyrinth holds a monstrous bull-headed jailer — the Minotaur restaged as a creature Theseus must pass on the way to war.

films.title: Minotaur, the Wild Beast of Crete
films.description: Italian peplum puts the beast in the title: the bull-man of the labyrinth as sword-and-sandal monster for Theseus to slay.

films.title: Minotaur
films.description: Tom Hardy descends into a Minoan labyrinth to kill the tribute-beast — a horror retelling that keeps the Minotaur as the labyrinth's hungry god.

music.title: The Minotaur
music.description: Birtwistle and Harsent give the bull-man speech in dream — the Minotaur as tragic half-human at Covent Garden, slain between Ariadne's plots and Theseus' blade.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: The Minotaur Asterius shares an Elysium boss arena with Theseus — the bull-man as reluctant champion, more honourable than his Athenian partner.

popCulture.title: Assassin's Creed Odyssey
popCulture.creator: Ubisoft Quebec
popCulture.description: The Minotaur waits as a legendary boss beneath Crete — the labyrinth beast restaged for open-world combat, with Theseus' thread still in the mission lore.

popCulture.title: The House of Asterion
popCulture.creator: Jorge Luis Borges
popCulture.description: Borges lets the Minotaur narrate his own house — the labyrinth as solitude, the bull-man waiting for the redeemer who will end him.

popCulture.title: The King Must Die
popCulture.creator: Mary Renault
popCulture.description: Renault's bull-court Crete rebuilds the Minotaur as ritual and politics — the beast at the heart of the tribute Theseus comes to end.
